angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 35,477,917 km at 97.37 pc = 4.87 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112716: distance 97.371 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.028), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 97.371 +/- 2.726 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 10.0171 +/- 0.1734 mas (same row, RUWE 1.65), 57.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 50.996 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112716: radius 50.996 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 543.303 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 35,477,917 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3905 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112716: effective temperature 3905 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.106) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112716: effective temperature 3905 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.106) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * tau Aqr: spectral type M0III (1989ApJS...71..245K)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 1081) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
